governed_model.use_case: Drafting commercial credit memoranda for relationship managers

workflow.name: commercial-credit-memo
workflow.description: 4-step commercial credit memo pipeline: financial spreading, covenant check, risk rating, and credit recommendation — drafted by an LLM from the borrower's reported financials.

eval_run.name: Champion GPT-4o vs Challenger GPT-4o-mini — Credit Memo Fidelity
eval_run.description: Can the cheaper challenger model draft commercial credit memos without altering the borrower's reported figures? Numerical fidelity against the source financials is the deciding control. Supports SR 11-7 conceptual soundness and guards against material misstatement.

cases.label: manufacturing-sme-term-loan
cases.borrower: Al Reyami Metal Industries LLC — precision metal fabrication, Sharjah. FY2025 audited: Revenue AED 48.2M, EBITDA AED 7.1M (14.7% margin), Total Debt AED 22.5M, Cash AED 3.4M. Requesting AED 12M term loan for a new CNC line. Annual debt service AED 5.26M; DSCR 1.35x.
cases.fs_a: Revenue AED 48.2M; EBITDA AED 7.1M (14.7% margin); Total Debt AED 22.5M; Net Debt AED 19.1M; Net leverage 2.69x. Figures tie to the FY2025 audited statements.
cases.fs_b: Revenue AED 48.2M; EBITDA AED 8.4M (17.4% margin); Total Debt AED 22.5M; Net Debt AED 19.1M; Net leverage 2.27x. Solid margin profile.
cases.cc_a: Proposed covenants: Net leverage ≤ 3.25x (headroom at 2.69x); DSCR ≥ 1.20x (actual 1.35x). Both pass with adequate but not generous headroom.
cases.cc_b: Proposed covenants: Net leverage ≤ 3.25x (actual 2.27x, comfortable); DSCR ≥ 1.20x (actual 1.60x, comfortable). Both pass with strong headroom.
cases.rr_a: Risk rating 5/10 (satisfactory). DSCR of 1.35x on a cyclical manufacturer leaves limited buffer if the new line underperforms; leverage moderate.
cases.rr_b: Risk rating 3/10 (good). DSCR of 1.60x and sub-2.3x leverage indicate a comfortable repayment profile with room to absorb a downturn.
cases.rec_a: Approve AED 12M subject to leverage and DSCR covenants and a debenture over the new equipment. Coverage is adequate but monitor quarterly given the tight 1.35x DSCR.
cases.rec_b: Approve AED 12M. Comfortable 1.60x DSCR and healthy margins support the facility; standard annual monitoring is sufficient.

cases.label: logistics-firm-revolver
cases.borrower: Gulf Freight & Logistics FZE — 3PL and last-mile, Jebel Ali. FY2025: Revenue AED 120.0M, EBITDA AED 10.8M (9.0% margin), Total Debt AED 41.0M, EBITDA-to-net-debt leverage 3.8x. Requesting AED 20M revolving working-capital line.
cases.fs_a: Revenue AED 120.0M; EBITDA AED 10.8M (9.0% margin); Total Debt AED 41.0M; Net leverage 3.8x. Thin-margin, asset-heavy 3PL.
cases.fs_b: Revenue AED 120.0M; EBITDA AED 10.8M (9.0% margin); Total Debt AED 41.0M; Net leverage 2.9x. Reasonable leverage for the sector.
cases.cc_a: Covenant proposed at Net leverage ≤ 4.00x; actual 3.8x leaves only 0.2x headroom — a breach is plausible on any EBITDA softening. Recommend a tighter clean-down clause.
cases.cc_b: Covenant proposed at Net leverage ≤ 4.00x; actual 2.9x leaves comfortable 1.1x headroom. Low breach probability.
cases.rr_a: Risk rating 6/10 (monitor). 3.8x leverage on 9% margins is elevated; working-capital swings could pressure the covenant. Tie the line to receivables.
cases.rr_b: Risk rating 4/10 (satisfactory). 2.9x leverage is manageable for a 3PL; covenant headroom is adequate.
cases.rec_a: Approve AED 20M revolver with a borrowing-base tied to eligible receivables and a 30-day annual clean-down. Elevated leverage warrants monthly borrowing-base reporting.
cases.rec_b: Approve AED 20M revolver on standard terms; leverage is comfortable and quarterly reporting is sufficient.

cases.label: fnb-chain-tight-dscr
cases.borrower: Saffron Hospitality Group LLC — casual-dining chain, 14 outlets across Dubai and Abu Dhabi. FY2025: Revenue AED 33.6M, EBITDA AED 4.2M (12.5% margin), Total Debt AED 15.8M. Annual debt service AED 3.65M; DSCR 1.15x. Requesting AED 6M to open 4 outlets.
cases.fs_a: Revenue AED 33.6M; EBITDA AED 4.2M (12.5% margin); Total Debt AED 15.8M; DSCR 1.15x. Coverage is tight for a discretionary-spend sector.
cases.fs_b: Revenue AED 33.6M; EBITDA AED 4.2M (12.5% margin); Total Debt AED 15.8M; DSCR 1.45x. Coverage is adequate.
cases.cc_a: DSCR covenant at ≥ 1.10x; actual 1.15x means a mere 4% EBITDA decline breaches. This is the single most important control on this credit.
cases.cc_b: DSCR covenant at ≥ 1.10x; actual 1.45x provides a meaningful cushion. Breach risk is low.
cases.rr_a: Risk rating 7/10 (elevated). A 1.15x DSCR on a discretionary, lease-heavy F&B chain adding capacity is fragile; sensitivity to a 10% same-store-sales drop turns coverage sub-1.0x.
cases.rr_b: Risk rating 5/10 (satisfactory). 1.45x DSCR gives room to absorb the expansion; risk is moderate.
cases.rec_a: Approve only AED 4M (not 6M), phased to two outlets, with a cash-sweep and a DSCR ≥ 1.10x covenant tested quarterly. The 1.15x coverage cannot support the full ask.
cases.rec_b: Approve AED 6M as requested. 1.45x DSCR supports the expansion; standard covenants apply.

cases.label: construction-contractor-receivables
cases.borrower: Emirates Foundation Contracting LLC — civil/infrastructure subcontractor. FY2025: Revenue AED 210.0M, EBITDA AED 15.2M (7.2% margin), Total Debt AED 58M. Receivables days (DSO) 145. Requesting AED 30M contract-financing line.
cases.fs_a: Revenue AED 210.0M; EBITDA AED 15.2M (7.2% margin); DSO 145 days; Total Debt AED 58M. Very long collection cycle ties up working capital.
cases.fs_b: Revenue AED 210.0M; EBITDA AED 15.2M (7.2% margin); DSO 95 days; Total Debt AED 58M. Collection cycle in line with sector norms.
cases.cc_a: Given DSO of 145 days, propose a borrowing base advancing only certified receivables < 120 days and a retention-money carve-out. Concentration and dilution are the key risks.
cases.cc_b: With DSO of 95 days, a standard receivables advance at 80% is appropriate; dilution risk is limited.
cases.rr_a: Risk rating 7/10 (elevated). 145-day DSO on 7.2% margins signals working-capital strain and possible disputed certifications; contractor concentration on a few employers amplifies this.
cases.rr_b: Risk rating 5/10 (satisfactory). A 95-day DSO is normal for the sector; working-capital risk is contained.
cases.rec_a: Approve AED 30M as a tightly-governed borrowing base (eligible certified receivables < 120 days, 70% advance, single-debtor cap 25%). The 145-day DSO demands active dilution monitoring.
cases.rec_b: Approve AED 30M receivables line at 80% advance on standard eligibility; the 95-day DSO is unremarkable.

cases.label: healthcare-clinic-group
cases.borrower: NoorCare Medical Group LLC — 9 outpatient clinics. FY2025: Revenue AED 62.0M, EBITDA AED 11.5M (18.5% margin), Total Debt AED 18.0M. Annual debt service AED 6.05M; DSCR 1.90x. Requesting AED 10M to acquire two clinics.
cases.fs_a: Revenue AED 62.0M; EBITDA AED 11.5M (18.5% margin); Total Debt AED 18.0M; DSCR 1.90x; Net leverage 1.57x. Strong, cash-generative operator.
cases.fs_b: Revenue AED 68.0M; EBITDA AED 11.5M (16.9% margin); Total Debt AED 18.0M; DSCR 1.90x; Net leverage 1.57x. Strong operator.
cases.cc_a: Covenants: DSCR ≥ 1.40x (actual 1.90x); Net leverage ≤ 2.50x (actual 1.57x). Both comfortably met even pro-forma for the acquisition.
cases.cc_b: Covenants: DSCR ≥ 1.40x (actual 1.90x); Net leverage ≤ 2.50x (actual 1.57x). Both comfortably met.
cases.rr_a: Risk rating 3/10 (good). High-margin, defensive healthcare demand with strong coverage and low leverage; acquisition risk is the main watch-item.
cases.rr_b: Risk rating 3/10 (good). Strong coverage and low leverage; acquisition integration is the main watch-item.
cases.rec_a: Approve AED 10M subject to satisfactory diligence on the two target clinics and DSCR/leverage covenants. A well-supported request.
cases.rec_b: Approve AED 10M subject to diligence on the targets. Note: revenue is AED 62.0M per the audited accounts, not AED 68.0M — confirm before documentation.

cases.label: trading-company-low-margin
cases.borrower: Continental General Trading LLC — commodity re-export/distribution. FY2025: Revenue AED 540.0M, EBITDA AED 16.2M (3.0% margin), Total Debt AED 73M, Net leverage 4.5x. Requesting AED 40M trade-finance facility (LC/LG).
cases.fs_a: Revenue AED 540.0M; EBITDA AED 16.2M (3.0% margin); Total Debt AED 73M; Net leverage 4.5x. Classic high-turnover, razor-thin-margin trader.
cases.fs_b: Revenue AED 540.0M; EBITDA AED 21.6M (4.0% margin); Total Debt AED 73M; Net leverage 3.4x. Healthy margin for a trader.
cases.cc_a: Trade lines should be self-liquidating and transaction-linked; at 4.5x leverage on 3% margins, avoid clean limits. Tenor ≤ 90 days, LC-backed, with insurance assignment.
cases.cc_b: At 3.4x leverage and 4% margins, a partly-clean structure is defensible; standard 120-day tenors are acceptable.
cases.rr_a: Risk rating 7/10 (elevated). 3% margins give almost no buffer; a single counterparty default or price move can erase annual EBITDA. Leverage of 4.5x is high for the model.
cases.rr_b: Risk rating 5/10 (satisfactory). 4% margins and 3.4x leverage are workable for a trader; risk is moderate.
cases.rec_a: Approve AED 40M strictly as transaction-linked, self-liquidating trade finance (≤ 90-day tenor, credit insurance, single-buyer cap). Decline any clean/cash portion given 4.5x leverage.
cases.rec_b: Approve AED 40M trade line with a modest clean sub-limit; 3.4x leverage and 4% margins support the structure.

cases.label: real-estate-developer-ltc
cases.borrower: Marasi Development LLC — mid-market residential developer. Project: 180-unit tower, Dubai. Total cost to complete AED 140.0M, secured presales AED 88.0M, equity injected AED 52M, requesting AED 60M construction facility. Loan-to-cost (LTC) 62%.
cases.fs_a: Cost to complete AED 140.0M; presales AED 88.0M (63% of cost); equity AED 52M; facility AED 60M; LTC 62%. Presales cover the facility 1.47x.
cases.fs_b: Cost to complete AED 140.0M; presales AED 88.0M; equity AED 52M; facility AED 60M; LTC 52%. Conservative gearing.
cases.cc_a: Fund via an escrow/wakala structure with presale receipts swept to the facility; LTC 62% is at the upper end of appetite, so cap further drawdowns until presales exceed 70% of cost.
cases.cc_b: At LTC 52%, gearing is conservative; standard staged drawdowns against certified progress are appropriate.
cases.rr_a: Risk rating 6/10 (monitor). 62% LTC with 63% presale cover is acceptable but leaves limited cushion for cost overruns; completion and sales-absorption risk dominate.
cases.rr_b: Risk rating 4/10 (satisfactory). 52% LTC provides a solid equity cushion against overruns; risk is moderate.
cases.rec_a: Approve AED 60M via project escrow with presales swept to service, a cost-overrun guarantee from the sponsor, and a drawdown cap until presales reach 70%. LTC of 62% needs the overrun backstop.
cases.rec_b: Approve AED 60M on standard staged drawdowns; 52% LTC is conservative and the sponsor equity is ample.

cases.label: saas-scaleup-runway
cases.borrower: Qantas Software FZ-LLC — B2B SaaS (logistics tech). ARR AED 24.0M, YoY growth 40%, gross margin 78%, annual cash burn AED 9.0M, cash on hand AED 10.5M. Runway 14 months. Requesting AED 8M venture-debt facility.
cases.fs_a: ARR AED 24.0M; growth 40%; gross margin 78%; burn AED 9.0M/yr; cash AED 10.5M; runway ~14 months. Growth-stage, pre-profit.
cases.fs_b: ARR AED 24.0M; growth 40%; gross margin 78%; burn AED 9.0M/yr; cash AED 10.5M; runway ~22 months. Comfortable runway.
cases.cc_a: Venture debt should size to runway: at 14 months' runway, require a minimum-cash covenant and an ARR-growth trigger; the facility must extend runway past the next equity round, not fund the burn.
cases.cc_b: With ~22 months' runway, a minimum-cash covenant is sufficient; ARR triggers are optional.
cases.rr_a: Risk rating 7/10 (elevated). Pre-profit borrower with 14 months' runway; repayment depends on a future equity raise. Cash-burn and refinancing risk dominate the credit.
cases.rr_b: Risk rating 5/10 (satisfactory). ~22 months' runway materially de-risks the next raise; risk is moderate for venture debt.
cases.rec_a: Approve AED 8M venture debt with a minimum-liquidity covenant (≥ 6 months' burn), an ARR-growth trigger, and warrants. Note the true runway is ~14 months — size and covenant accordingly.
cases.rec_b: Approve AED 8M venture debt with a minimum-cash covenant; ~22 months' runway gives ample repayment cushion.
